calls.head: The matchup inside the matchup
calls.body: The Red Wings are near the top of the league for the power play, but the Golden Knights are the best at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Red Wings’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots.
calls.call: The Red Wings’ power play creates more than the league-average 7.7 expected goals per 60 against the Golden Knights.

calls.happened: On the power play, Detroit had 13.7 expected goals per 60 tonight, against a league average of 7.7 expected goals per 60. They usually sit at 8.8 expected goals per 60.

calls.title: The chances came, the goals didn’t
calls.plain: The Red Wings beat the league average on the power play, even against the Golden Knights. They didn’t score on it, though: 0 for 2.
calls.said: the Red Wings’ power play would win the standoff with the Golden Knights’ kill

calls.head: Like for like: Kolesar vs. Dowd
calls.body: At home, the Red Wings keep sending Kolesar’s line (Mazur, Dries and Kolesar) out against opponents’ fourth lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Todd McLellan keeps choosing line for line. Tonight the Golden Knights’ fourth line is Lavoie, Dowd and Gatcomb.
calls.call: The Red Wings’ L4 (Mazur, Dries and Kolesar) spends at least 30% of its 5-on-5 time against the Golden Knights’ fourth line, against about 18% with no line matching.
calls.nums: At home: 42% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against fourth lines, about 18% with no line matching

With no line matching, this group would face fourth lines about 18% of the time, about as often as those lines are on the ice.

calls.head: Expect the Golden Knights to have the puck more
calls.body: The Golden Knights have been one of the league’s best at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Red Wings around the middle. Expect the Golden Knights to spend more of the night in the Red Wings’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

surprises.head: Detroit shortened their bench
surprises.body: Detroit’s bottom-six forwards played 36% of the forwards’ 5-on-5 time, against their usual 42% and a league average of 42%. A team strays this far about once every 40 games.

story.head: Connelly scores with less than two minutes left to lift the Golden Knights
paras: Anton Johansson struck first for the Red Wings early in the third, but Braeden Bowman made it 1-1 for Vegas a little over two minutes later. Trevor Connelly put the Golden Knights ahead for good with less than two minutes left.

The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. Carter Hart made 25 saves for the Golden Knights, and Daniil Tarasov stopped 32 of 34 at the other end. The Knights moved to 11-5-2, second in the Pacific, while the Red Wings fell to 7-7-3, still last in the Atlantic.

items.text: Keegan Kolesar played his first game against Vegas since leaving.
Victor Olofsson has a point in all five games this season.
Mitch Marner’s eleven-game point streak ended.
The Golden Knights have beaten the Red Wings four straight times, going back to the 2024-25 season.
